scope: Frontend and accessibility review only. No UI framework or first platform is approved, so this record defines adapter-neutral interaction and verification contracts without claiming implemented behavior.

dependencyEvidence.sharedBoundary: The desktop UI consumes the shared download domain and may present or request transitions, but must not redefine download state, retry, resume, cancellation, destination-conflict, or recovery rules.

primaryActions.accessibleOutcome: Focus moves to the created download or an actionable validation error; the chosen destination is exposed by name.
The item exposes paused status and a resume action.
The item exposes active status, or a clear explanation and restart choice when safe resume is unavailable.
A confirmation states the approved partial-file consequence; focus returns to a stable location.
The item exposes queued or active status without losing the preceding failure explanation.
The platform file reveal action has an accessible name containing the file name.

interactionContract.destinationConflict: Present overwrite, rename, and cancel only if approved by product policy. Name the existing destination, explain consequences, and do not rely on color alone.
interactionContract.restartRecovery: Recovered items retain their durable domain state. Interrupted items expose whether resume or explicit restart is available; partial files are never announced as completed.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Every core action is reachable and operable by keyboard with a logical focus order and no keyboard trap.
accessibilityRequirements.verification: Runtime keyboard traversal and activation on each approved platform.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Focus is visibly distinguishable in default, high-contrast, and forced-color modes and is restored after dialogs or item removal.
accessibilityRequirements.verification: Runtime visual inspection plus platform contrast tooling.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Controls expose stable accessible names, roles, values, disabled state, and state-specific actions; icon-only controls have text alternatives.
accessibilityRequirements.verification: Accessibility-tree inspection and platform screen-reader scenarios.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Progress exposes determinate value when total size is known and an indeterminate/busy state otherwise; status changes are announced without repeating every progress tick.
accessibilityRequirements.verification: Accessibility-tree and screen-reader testing during a controlled transfer.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Errors identify the affected download, explain the recoverable next step, and remain available for review after announcement.
accessibilityRequirements.verification: Runtime failure scenarios for network loss, insufficient storage, invalid URL, and unsupported resume.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Text and essential graphics meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast expectations, support text scaling, and do not clip at the platform's approved scaling range.
accessibilityRequirements.verification: Automated contrast checks plus runtime inspection at approved scale settings.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Motion is nonessential, avoids progress-animation dependence, and respects the platform reduced-motion preference.
accessibilityRequirements.verification: Runtime comparison with reduced motion disabled and enabled.

accessibilityRequirements.requirement: Status, selection, failure, and completion are conveyed with text or semantics in addition to color, shape, or animation.

runtimeAcceptanceScenarios.scenario: Keyboard-only user adds a valid URL and destination, observes queued then active progress, pauses, resumes, completes, and locates the file.
requiredEvidence: real application DOM or native accessibility tree

runtimeAcceptanceScenarios.scenario: Keyboard-only user cancels a queued, active, and paused item and receives the approved partial-file consequence before confirming.
requiredEvidence: real application DOM or native accessibility tree

runtimeAcceptanceScenarios.scenario: Network loss interrupts an active download; the user retries or is offered explicit restart when safe resume is unavailable.
Application restart restores queued, paused, completed, failed, and interrupted items without announcing partial files as complete.
A destination conflict is resolved through each approved choice without pointer input or color-only information.
Core flow is repeated with high contrast, text scaling, and reduced motion enabled.

usabilityPlan.participants: Recruit representative users from the human-approved primary segment, including keyboard-only and screen-reader users where feasible; record any coverage gap as a limitation.
tasks: Add a download and choose a destination
measures: time on task as descriptive evidence
usabilityPlan.limitations: Do not generalize qualitative findings statistically; retain contradictory evidence and separate observation, participant statement, interpretation, and assumption.

traceability.limitation: Platform-specific execution awaits approved first platform, UI stack, and supported versions.
No participant research evidence is present; this plan does not claim findings.

blockedBy: Human-approved primary segment and first platform
Approved bounded MVP and cancellation/conflict policies
Selected UI technology and supported OS versions
Available shared download-domain API from downstream implementation
exitEvidence: UI implementation consuming the shared domain service
real runtime keyboard and accessibility-tree tests

knownRisks: A premature UI implementation could encode unapproved product policies or duplicate shared-domain business rules.
Cross-platform framework accessibility behavior cannot be inferred from source code and must be tested on every approved platform.
Frequent progress announcements can overwhelm assistive-technology users; announcement throttling needs runtime tuning without hiding meaningful state changes.
No application runtime exists in the repository, so user-visible behavioral evidence cannot yet be produced.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
